audit.whatIsWrong: First item reads Skill and Two+ items reads Fiora, while the whys[] for both stages argue Sion outright.
audit.why: The packet chart gives Sion both stages and the already-audited mirror recorded the same flip ('First item -> Sion, 2+ items -> Sion'). whys[5] and whys[6] already say your HP pool outpaces vital damage and you win the final brawl, so only the tokens disagreed.
audit.corrected: First item and Two+ items to Sion as matched full/content pairs, with those two ratings raised and phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to state why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is the tracked ability in seven different fields and its cooldown appears nowhere; Lunge and Grand Challenge are likewise unnumbered.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s — the longest basic cooldown in her kit and the entire reason a baited parry is worth so much. Lunge is 13s at rank 1, so she cannot reposition freely early. Grand Challenge is 110/90/70s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, phases[5].why and wants.you[0] now carry Riposte's 24s; whys[0] gives Lunge's 13s; whys[4] gives the 110s ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry describes Riposte as 'parries + stuns' as though the stun is unconditional, and tells you to bait it without saying what actually triggers it.
audit.why: Riot's text: the stab slows the first champion hit, OR stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with it. Releasing a charged Decimating Smash into an active Riposte is what upgrades her parry into a stun on you — the single decisive interaction in this lane, and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, whys[2], wants.you[0] and wants.foe[1] all restated around the condition: feed it no CC and it is only a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grand Challenge's heal was described as affecting only Fiora, and Bladework never appeared at all.
audit.why: Grand Challenge heals Fiora AND her allies in the area — in a teamfight that is the difference between a duel and a group swing. Bladework's second attack is a guaranteed crit after the first slows, which is what makes her short trades so lopsided.
audit.corrected: whys[4] states the ally heal and the 110s cooldown; whys[2] names Bladework's crit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer mentions anti-heal in itemisation, but the content layer never tells you when it decides a fight.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal on both Duelist's Dance and Grand Challenge — the exact two sources that undo the long fights this entry tells you to force at two items.
audit.corrected: late now puts Grievous Wounds ahead of the extended fight.

edits.before: This is where the matchup flips. Your Heartsteel stacks and max-HP passive compound into a pool so large that even Fiora's percent-true vital damage becomes a slow grind — she cannot burst you in a single rotation. Use your E armor-shred to punish her low armor base in extended fights, and remember your zombie passive (Glory in Death) forces her to stay and keep fighting after your death or surrender the wave, draining her HP even on trades she wins. At 2+ items you are nearly unkillable in a straight brawl and can use R to gap-close if she tries to disengage once her Riposte is spent. The lane is ultimately decided by whose execution is cleaner across the full game; the stat line at 50% reflects exactly that.
edits.after: This is where the matchup flips. Your Heartsteel stacks and max-HP passive compound into a pool so large that Fiora's vital damage becomes a slow grind — she cannot burst you in a single rotation. Use Roar of the Slayer's armour shred in extended fights, and have Grievous Wounds bought before you start one, because her vitals and Grand Challenge both heal her back. Glory in Death forces her to keep fighting after your death or surrender the wave, draining her even on trades she wins. At 2+ items you are nearly unkillable in a straight brawl and can R to close if she disengages once Riposte is spent. The lane is decided by whose execution is cleaner.

notes: The decisive interaction was half-stated everywhere: Riposte only becomes a STUN if it blocks an immobilizing effect. Releasing a charged Decimating Smash into an active parry is what arms it — feed it nothing and it is a slow. Riposte's 24s at rank 1 is also the longest cooldown in her kit and was never given, so 'bait it' had no price attached. Per the mirror, I did not assert whether Sion is unstoppable during the charge or whether a Riposte stun can stop it — Riot's text does not say.
